quick_reference: CLINICIAN QUICK REFERENCE — HCC RAF GUIDE | CMS-HCC V28 | Medicare Advantage 2026
Use this sheet at point of care. Each condition must be documented annually using MEAT criteria (Monitor · Evaluate · Assess/Address · Treat)

Monitor: Tumor markers, imaging surveillance, metastatic sites
Evaluate: Number/location of metastases, treatment response
Assess: Functional status, pain control, hospice candidacy
Treat: Chemotherapy, radiation, palliative care
⚠️ Use secondary site codes (C77–C79) WITH primary site code. Do not use C80.1 if primary site is known.

Monitor: O2 sat, dyspnea scale, imaging
Evaluate: Stage (TNM), histology, treatment response
Assess: Performance status (ECOG), surgical candidacy
Treat: Chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation
⚠️ Document laterality (right/left) and lobe. Specify small cell vs non-small cell when known.

Monitor: CD4 count, viral load trends, opportunistic infections
Evaluate: Current HIV stage, ARV response, resistance testing
Assess: Treatment adherence, drug interactions, comorbidities
Treat: Antiretroviral therapy (ARV), prophylaxis
⚠️ Document "HIV disease" (B20) not just "HIV status" — specify active disease vs asymptomatic (Z21)

Monitor: Neurological exam, functional level (ASIA scale)
Evaluate: Level of injury (cervical/thoracic), completeness
Assess: Complications: pressure ulcers, UTIs, autonomic dysreflexia
Treat: PT/OT, pressure offloading, bladder management
⚠️ Quadriplegia (G82.5x) has HIGHEST RAF in motor function category (0.890). Document level and completeness explicitly.

Monitor: CBC trends, lymph node exam, B symptoms
Evaluate: Disease stage, bone marrow involvement, LDH
Assess: Treatment phase (induction, remission, relapse)
Treat: Chemo, targeted therapy, stem cell transplant
⚠️ Specify type: Hodgkin vs NHL vs leukemia vs myeloma. Document remission status explicitly.

Monitor: Wound measurements (length, width, depth), photography
Evaluate: Stage 4 = full thickness, bone/tendon/muscle exposed
Assess: Infection signs, nutritional status, pressure offloading
Treat: Wound debridement, specialty wound care, surgery
⚠️ MUST document STAGE 4 explicitly — staging is clinical. Unspecified pressure ulcer (L89.x09) does NOT generate payment HCC. Photograph and measure at each visit.

Monitor: CEA levels, colonoscopy interval, stoma if present
Evaluate: Stage, surgical margins, metastatic status
Assess: Recurrence risk, surveillance schedule
Treat: Surgery, chemo, radiation
⚠️ Document primary site specifically (cecum, ascending, sigmoid, rectum). Use C19 for rectosigmoid junction.

Monitor: Motor/sensory exam, functional mobility
Evaluate: Etiology (stroke, trauma, MS, tumor), completeness
Assess: Spasticity, pain, contractures, fall risk
Treat: PT/OT, antispasmodics, AFO/orthotics
⚠️ Specify paraplegia (G82.2x) vs hemiplegia (G81.x) vs monoplegia. Document dominant vs non-dominant side for hemiplegia.

Monitor: Seizure log, EEG results, medication levels
Evaluate: Seizure type (generalized tonic-clonic, status epilepticus)
Assess: Breakthrough seizures, medication compliance
Treat: Antiepileptic drugs, rescue medications, neurology co-management
⚠️ Status epilepticus (G41.x) maps to highest-RAF epilepsy HCC (0.567). Document seizure type specifically — "convulsions unspecified" (R56.9) does NOT map to payment HCC in V28.

Monitor: EDSS score, relapse frequency, MRI intervals
Evaluate: Disease course (RRMS, PPMS, SPMS), disability level
Assess: Bladder/bowel, cognitive, fatigue, depression
Treat: Disease-modifying therapies (interferons, natalizumab)
⚠️ G35 is the only ICD-10 code for MS. Always document current disease activity and functional status to support medical necessity.

Monitor: Wound size, depth, slough/eschar, surrounding skin
Evaluate: Stage 3 = full thickness, subcutaneous tissue visible
Assess: Offloading compliance, nutrition (albumin, prealbumin)
Treat: Wound dressings, debridement, nutrition supplementation
⚠️ Must document STAGE 3. Specify anatomical site (sacrum L89.15x, heel L89.61x, etc.). Stage must be documented by clinician — cannot be assumed from nursing notes alone.
Chronic Ulcer of Skin / Non-Pressure Ulcer

Monitor: Wound location, dimensions, drainage, granulation
Evaluate: Etiology: venous (L97.x), arterial, diabetic, other
Assess: Healing trajectory, vascular assessment
Treat: Compression (venous), wound care, vascular referral
⚠️ Specify ulcer type and location: lower leg (L97.x), other site (L98.4x). Diabetic foot ulcer is captured under diabetes HCC (E11.621) — do not double-code.

Monitor: Vital signs, fever, lactate, culture results
Evaluate: Source of infection, organ dysfunction (SOFA score)
Assess: Sepsis severity — confirm meets Sepsis-3 criteria
Treat: IV antibiotics, vasopressors, fluid resuscitation
⚠️ Specify organism when known. R65.20/R65.21 requires underlying infection code first. Document septic shock separately.

Monitor: LFTs, INR, albumin, bilirubin, ascites monitoring
Evaluate: Child-Pugh or MELD score, varices, encephalopathy
Assess: Decompensation status, transplant candidacy
Treat: Diuretics, lactulose, rifaximin, paracentesis
⚠️ Document CIRRHOSIS explicitly — "liver disease" alone insufficient. Specify with/without ascites for K70.30 vs K70.31.

Monitor: Tumor markers, surveillance imaging, specialist notes
Evaluate: Stage, receptor status (breast), Gleason (prostate)
Assess: Treatment response, surgical status
Treat: Surgery, hormone therapy, radiation
⚠️ Always document organ/site specifically. Confirm active vs history of cancer — history codes (Z85.x) do NOT generate RAF.

Monitor: CBC with differential, reticulocyte count
Evaluate: Aplastic vs hypoplastic, bone marrow biopsy results
Assess: Transfusion dependence, transplant candidacy
Treat: Immunosuppression, transfusions, stem cell transplant
⚠️ "Anemia unspecified" (D64.9) has NO payment HCC in V28. Must specify aplastic (D61.x) or acquired hemolytic (D59.x).
Cardio-Respiratory Failure and Shock / Cardiac Arrest

Monitor: Post-resuscitation vitals, cardiac monitoring
Evaluate: Underlying cause, cardiac function post-arrest
Assess: Neurological outcome, ICD candidacy
Treat: ACLS, ICD placement, cardiac rehab
⚠️ Use I46.2 (underlying cardiac condition) or I46.9 (unspecified). Document cause and survival status clearly.

Monitor: Positive/negative symptom scale (PANSS), med compliance
Evaluate: Psychotic symptoms, functional level, housing
Assess: Relapse risk, side effects (EPS, metabolic)
Treat: Antipsychotics, LAI, case management
⚠️ Specify schizophrenia TYPE and episode status. Schizoaffective (F25.x) maps to same HCC. Document acute exacerbation vs stable.

Monitor: Joint exam, ESR/CRP/RF/anti-CCP, medication labs
Evaluate: Disease activity (DAS28), functional class
Assess: Response to biologics, cardiovascular risk
Treat: DMARDs, biologics, corticosteroids
⚠️ Specify seropositive (M05) vs seronegative (M06). Document organ involvement for highest specificity.

Monitor: Transplanted organ function labs, immunosuppression levels
Evaluate: Rejection episodes, organ function (GFR for kidney)
Assess: Infection risk, malignancy surveillance
Treat: Immunosuppressants (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, MMF)
⚠️ Document transplant STATUS (Z94.x) at EVERY visit — it must be recaptured annually. Kidney (Z94.0), heart (Z94.1), lung (Z94.2), liver (Z94.4). Must be active — not rejected/failed.

Monitor: Seizure frequency, medication levels, compliance
Evaluate: Seizure type (focal, absence, myoclonic)
Assess: Driving restrictions, fall risk, triggers
Treat: Antiepileptic drugs, lifestyle modification
⚠️ Use G40.x codes — specify intractable vs not intractable, with/without status epilepticus. Unspecified codes generate lower or no RAF.

Monitor: PHQ-9 ≥15, suicidality assessment at each visit
Evaluate: Severe MDD with or without psychotic features
Assess: Functional impairment, hospitalization risk
Treat: Antidepressants (high dose), ECT, psychiatric co-management
⚠️ V28 KEY SPLIT: Severe MDD (F32.2, F32.3, F33.2, F33.3) generates RAF 0.396. Mild/moderate = lower RAF 0.214. MUST document severity with PHQ-9 score.

Monitor: AUDIT-C or AUDIT score at each visit, LFTs
Evaluate: Severity: mild/moderate/severe use disorder
Assess: Withdrawal risk, co-occurring mental health
Treat: Brief intervention, naltrexone/acamprosate, AA referral
⚠️ Document DEPENDENCE (F10.2x) for highest RAF vs abuse (F10.1x). Must specify with/without withdrawal or intoxication.

Monitor: Urine drug screen, PDMP check, injection site exam
Evaluate: Substance type, severity, tolerance/withdrawal
Assess: Overdose risk, co-occurring Hep C/HIV
Treat: MAT (buprenorphine, methadone), naloxone Rx
⚠️ Specify substance: opioid (F11.x) has distinct codes. Document DEPENDENCE vs abuse. "Opioid use disorder" must map to F11.2x for payment.

Monitor: Stump exam, prosthetic fit, phantom pain assessment
Evaluate: Amputation level, laterality, acquired vs congenital
Assess: Rehabilitation status, functional mobility
Treat: Prosthetics, pain management, PT referral
⚠️ Use Z89.x codes — specify level (below-knee Z89.51x, above-knee Z89.61x, etc.) and laterality. Must document ACQUIRED amputation — congenital absence is different code.

Monitor: CBC, hemoglobin, reticulocyte count, bilirubin
Evaluate: Hemolysis cause (autoimmune, sickle cell, thalassemia)
Assess: Crisis frequency, organ damage, hydrops
Treat: Steroids, transfusions, hydroxyurea (sickle cell)
⚠️ Specify type — sickle cell disease (D57.x) carries high RAF. Must document crisis status when applicable.

Monitor: NIHSS score, neurological deficits, fall risk
Evaluate: Infarct location, etiology (cardioembolic, atherosclerotic)
Assess: Disability level, aphasia, dysphagia, neglect
Treat: Antiplatelet/anticoagulation, statins, PT/OT/speech
⚠️ Use I63.x for ischemic stroke (highest RAF). I64 for unspecified. TIA (G45.x) does NOT map to stroke HCC. Document neurological deficits at each follow-up visit.

Monitor: CMAI scale for agitation, behavioral log
Evaluate: Type of behavioral disturbance (agitation, psychosis, wandering)
Assess: Safety risk, caregiver burden, medication side effects
Treat: Antipsychotics (with caution), environment modifications
⚠️ HIGH VALUE: Must document SPECIFIC behavioral disturbance — "with agitation" (F01.511), "with psychotic disturbance" (F01.52). Plain "dementia" = lower RAF.

Monitor: Spirometry (FEV1/FVC), O2 sat, exacerbation log
Evaluate: GOLD stage (1–4), symptom burden (CAT/mMRC)
Assess: Inhaler technique, smoking status, vaccination
Treat: SABA/LAMA/ICS-LABA, pulmonary rehab, O2 if indicated
⚠️ Specify COPD (J44.x) not just "lung disease" — J44.1 (with acute exacerbation) is most specific. Emphysema (J43.x) and chronic bronchitis (J41-42) also map to same HCC.

Monitor: Sleep study results, daytime somnolence, O2 monitoring
Evaluate: OHS (BMI + hypercapnia + hypoventilation) vs OSA alone
Assess: Respiratory failure risk, BiPAP compliance
Treat: BiPAP/CPAP, weight loss, sleep medicine referral
⚠️ OSA alone (G47.33) does NOT generate payment HCC in V28. Must have OBESITY HYPOVENTILATION (E66.2) with hypercapnia confirmed on ABG. Different from OSA.

Monitor: Daily weight, edema, dyspnea scale, BNP/NT-proBNP
Evaluate: EF% (systolic vs diastolic), NYHA class, volume status
Assess: Medication tolerance, acute decompensation episodes
Treat: Diuretics, ACE/ARB/ARNI, beta-blockers, SGLT2i
⚠️ Specify SYSTOLIC (I50.2x) vs DIASTOLIC (I50.3x) vs COMBINED (I50.4x). Document ACUTE vs CHRONIC. Acute on chronic = highest acuity code.

Monitor: GAD-7, PCL-5 (PTSD), Y-BOCS (OCD) scores at visits
Evaluate: Anxiety type (GAD, panic, PTSD, OCD), severity
Assess: Functional impairment, avoidance behaviors
Treat: SSRIs/SNRIs, CBT/exposure therapy, psychiatry referral
⚠️ MOST COMMONLY MISSED HCC in primary care (RAF 0.302). Specify: GAD (F41.1), panic disorder (F41.0), PTSD (F43.10/F43.11), OCD (F42.x). "Anxiety NOS" (F41.9) still valid but use specific code.

Monitor: UPDRS score, fall risk, medication timing
Evaluate: Stage (H&Y scale), ON/OFF fluctuations, dyskinesia
Assess: Non-motor symptoms: dementia, psychosis, autonomic
Treat: Levodopa/carbidopa, dopamine agonists, DBS referral
⚠️ Use G20.A1/A2 (without dyskinesia) or G20.C1/C2 (with dyskinesia). Old code G20 alone still valid but less specific.

Monitor: LFTs, viral load (HBV/HCV), fibrosis markers
Evaluate: Genotype, stage of fibrosis, treatment response
Assess: Progression to cirrhosis, treatment candidacy
Treat: Antivirals (DAAs for HCV, entecavir for HBV)
⚠️ Document viral type (B18.0, B18.1, B18.2). Cured HCV does NOT generate RAF — must be active or chronic.

Monitor: Extremity exam, duplex ultrasound intervals
Evaluate: DVT location, chronicity, post-thrombotic syndrome
Assess: Anticoagulation duration, bleeding risk
Treat: Anticoagulation (DOAC/warfarin), compression therapy
⚠️ Must use CHRONIC DVT codes (I82.x1/x2/x3) — acute DVT codes are different. Specify laterality and vessel.

Monitor: Troponin trends, EKG, chest pain monitoring
Evaluate: STEMI vs NSTEMI, wall motion abnormality, EF post-MI
Assess: Door-to-balloon time met, revascularization status
Treat: Dual antiplatelet, statin, beta-blocker, ACE
⚠️ Document STEMI vs NSTEMI vs subsequent MI (I22.x). Within 4 weeks = acute MI. After 4 weeks = use "old MI" or CAD codes.

Monitor: Holter/event monitor, ICD interrogation
Evaluate: VT morphology, substrate (ischemic vs non-ischemic)
Assess: Hemodynamic stability, ICD shocks delivered
Treat: Antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, sotalol), ICD, ablation
⚠️ Document SUSTAINED vs unsustained VT. I47.21 (sustained VT) is most specific. VFib (I49.01) maps to same HCC.

Monitor: Mood diary, sleep log, PHQ-9 and MDQ screens
Evaluate: Current episode: manic/depressed/mixed, severity
Assess: Medication levels (lithium, valproate), cycling frequency
Treat: Mood stabilizers, antipsychotics, therapy
⚠️ Always document CURRENT episode type. "Bipolar unspecified" (F31.9) still maps but be specific: manic (F31.1x), depressed (F31.3x), mixed (F31.6x).

Monitor: Adaptive behavior scales, communication assessment
Evaluate: ASD level (1/2/3 requiring support), IQ if tested
Assess: Behavioral interventions, school/employment status
Treat: ABA therapy, speech, OT, medication if needed
⚠️ F84.0 (autistic disorder) and F84.5 (Asperger's) both map. Document LEVEL of support required (Level 1/2/3) per DSM-5.

Monitor: GFR every 3 months, potassium, phosphorus, PTH
Evaluate: Stage 5 (GFR <15) or ESRD (on dialysis/Z99.2)
Assess: Dialysis access, transplant candidacy, AV fistula
Treat: Nephrology co-management, dialysis, transplant evaluation
⚠️ Must document ESRD (N18.6) or Stage 5 (N18.5) explicitly. Dialysis dependence = Z99.2. Any of these maps to HCC 326 (RAF 0.280).

Monitor: PHQ-9 score (mild 5–9, moderate 10–14)
Evaluate: Episode type (single vs recurrent), remission status
Assess: Functional impact, social support, safety
Treat: Antidepressants, therapy referral, follow-up plan
⚠️ Document severity using PHQ-9 score. "Depression NOS" or "depressive disorder unspecified" (F32.A) may no longer qualify. Specify mild (F32.0) or moderate (F32.1).

Monitor: Interpersonal function, behavioral patterns
Evaluate: Personality disorder type, co-occurring conditions
Assess: Treatment resistance, safety (self-harm risk)
Treat: DBT/CBT therapy, medication management
⚠️ Only paranoid (F60.0) and schizoid (F60.1) currently map to payment HCC. Other personality disorders may not generate V28 RAF.

Monitor: Weight, BMI at every visit, comorbidities
Evaluate: BMI ≥40 required, obesity-related complications
Assess: Readiness for weight loss interventions
Treat: Behavioral counseling, medications, bariatric referral
⚠️ Use E66.01 for morbid obesity. General obesity (E66.09, E66.9) may not meet threshold. Also code BMI (Z68.4x).

Monitor: Cognitive screening (MMSE/MoCA) at each visit
Evaluate: Dementia type and severity (mild/moderate/severe)
Assess: ADL/IADL function, safety, driving capability
Treat: Cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, caregiver support
⚠️ Document dementia TYPE (Alzheimer's G30.x, Lewy Body G31.83, Vascular F01.x, Frontotemporal G31.0x). "Senility" or "cognitive decline" insufficient for HCC.

Monitor: Neurological exam, carotid duplex intervals, BP control
Evaluate: Degree of stenosis, occlusion vs stenosis
Assess: Stroke risk (ABCD2 score), stent/endarterectomy status
Treat: Antiplatelet, statin, BP control, vascular surgery referral
⚠️ Document stenosis LOCATION specifically: carotid (I65.2x), vertebral (I65.0), cerebral (I66.x). Specify laterality. Sequelae of stroke (I69.x) also maps.

Monitor: Angina frequency, exertional tolerance, stress test
Evaluate: Stable vs unstable angina, coronary anatomy
Assess: Revascularization status, stent patency
Treat: Nitrates, beta-blockers, statin, antiplatelet
⚠️ V28 CRITICAL: CAD WITHOUT angina (I25.10) no longer maps to a payment HCC. MUST document angina symptoms to use I25.11x codes.

Monitor: Rate control check, HR at visits, CHA₂DS₂-VASc
Evaluate: AFib type (paroxysmal/persistent/permanent), rhythm status
Assess: Anticoagulation appropriateness, bleeding risk
Treat: Rate/rhythm control, anticoagulation (DOAC/warfarin)
⚠️ Always document AFib TYPE: paroxysmal (I48.0), persistent (I48.11/I48.19), permanent (I48.21). Unspecified (I48.91) still valid but be specific.

Monitor: HbA1c, blood glucose log, ketone testing
Evaluate: Acute complication type: DKA (E11.10/11) or hyperosmolar (E11.00/01)
Assess: Precipitating cause, hospital admissions for DKA
Treat: Insulin adjustment, hydration, hospitalization if needed
⚠️ DKA (E1x.10/11) and hyperosmolarity (E1x.00/01) are ACUTE complication codes = HCC 35. Same RAF as HCC 36/37 in V28 (constrained). Still important to document accurately.

Monitor: HbA1c, microalbumin, foot exam, dilated eye exam
Evaluate: Type of chronic complication (retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy)
Assess: Complication severity, progression, specialist involvement
Treat: Medication adjustment, referrals (ophthalmology, podiatry, nephrology)
⚠️ V28 CONSTRAINT: HCC 36 (chronic complications) = same RAF 0.166 as uncomplicated DM. STILL document complications for accurate clinical picture and comorbidity interactions.

Monitor: HbA1c, fasting glucose, BP, lipids
Evaluate: DM type (1, 2, LADA, drug-induced, other)
Assess: Glycemic control, medication tolerance
Treat: Metformin/insulin/GLP-1/SGLT2i per type and target
⚠️ Even "uncomplicated" diabetes generates RAF 0.166 in V28. Always specify TYPE (E10=Type1, E11=Type2, E08=underlying condition, E09=drug-induced).

Monitor: ABI (ankle-brachial index), pulse exam, wound check
Evaluate: Severity: claudication vs critical limb ischemia
Assess: Revascularization candidacy, wound healing
Treat: Antiplatelet, statin, cilostazol, vascular referral
⚠️ I73.9 (PVD unspecified) is valid but document symptoms: claudication, rest pain, tissue loss for higher specificity.

Monitor: GFR every 3–6 months, anemia, PTH, phosphorus
Evaluate: GFR 15–29 = Stage 4 — document with calculation
Assess: Rate of decline, cardiovascular risk, dialysis planning
Treat: Nephrology referral, anemia management, dietary restriction
⚠️ N18.4 (Stage 4 CKD) = RAF 0.137. Must use the specific stage code — "CKD unspecified" (N18.9) does NOT generate payment HCC in V28.

Monitor: MoCA/MMSE trending, patient-reported memory concerns
Evaluate: Distinguish from dementia — functional impact
Assess: Modifiable risk factors (sleep, exercise, vascular)
Treat: Lifestyle interventions, neurology referral if progressing
⚠️ G31.84 (mild cognitive impairment) and F06.70/F06.71 qualify. "Memory loss" unspecified (R41.3) does NOT map to HCC in V28.

Monitor: GFR every 6–12 months, BP, microalbumin
Evaluate: Stage 3a (GFR 45–59) vs 3b (GFR 30–44)
Assess: Progression risk, ACE/ARB therapy optimization
Treat: BP control, ACE/ARB, dietary sodium/protein reduction
⚠️ Only Stage 3b (N18.32) maps to HCC 328. Stage 3a (N18.31) and Stage 3 unspecified (N18.30) do NOT generate payment HCC in V28.

v28_traps: V28 TRAPS — CONDITIONS THAT NO LONGER GENERATE RAF IN 2026
These are commonly documented by primary care but generate ZERO RAF under V28. Stop relying on them — use better-specified codes where available.
V28 removed CAD codes that lack angina — clinical overlap with simple atherosclerosis
Use I25.11x (with angina) if angina present
✏️ Document ANGINA symptoms specifically at each visit
Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure
Hypertension without HF does not predict high cost in updated V28 data
Use I11.0 (with heart failure) if HF present
✏️ If patient has HF + HTN, use I11.0 — it maps to HCC 85
Removed — must have HF component to map
✏️ Document HF if present to qualify for I13.0 (HCC 85)
Removed from V28 — was heavily upcoded without clinical support in MA
❌ No longer generates RAF — focus on other documented comorbidities
✏️ Use E43 (severe) if clinically appropriate and documented
History of MI alone no longer sufficient in V28 without active management
Use active CAD codes (I25.11x) with angina
✏️ Document current CAD management and angina if present
Chronic total occlusion of coronary artery
None — document CAD with angina if symptomatic
✏️ Document angina or ischemic symptoms to qualify I25.11x
Hypertension alone has NEVER had a payment HCC — common misconception
Only qualifies when WITH heart failure (I11.0) or CKD (I12.x/I13.x)
❌ Do not list as HCC — only document to explain I11.0/I12.x/I13.x coding
Hyperlipidemia has no payment HCC — common misconception in primary care
❌ Document for clinical accuracy but adds no RAF value
OSA removed from V28 payment HCCs — it does not predict high cost alone
✏️ Order ABG if OSA + morbid obesity — E66.2 maps to HCC 221 (0.330)
Hypothyroidism has no payment HCC in any version
❌ Document for clinical care but adds no RAF value
Osteoarthritis has no payment HCC in V28
❌ Document RA (M05/M06) or other inflammatory arthritis if present — those DO map (HCC 40)
GERD has no payment HCC in any model
❌ Focus on documenting other conditions with payment HCCs
Osteoporosis without fracture has no payment HCC in V28
M80.x (with fracture) may qualify depending on site
✏️ If pathological fracture present, M80.x may generate RAF
Unspecified depression no longer reliably generates payment HCC in V28
⚠️ CRITICAL: MUST specify severity using PHQ-9. "Depression NOS" insufficient in V28.
Memory loss unspecified does not map to dementia HCC in V28
G31.84 (MCI) or F03.x (dementia) if criteria met
✏️ If patient meets criteria, diagnose and document dementia type/severity explicitly
❌ Document underlying causes (depression F32.x, anxiety F41.x) which DO have HCCs
Personal history of other endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases

interactions: V28 INTERACTION TERMS — BONUS RAF WHEN CONDITIONS CO-EXIST
These ADDITIVE bonuses apply ON TOP of each individual HCC coefficient when certain conditions are present together. Document ALL qualifying conditions at every visit.
💡 Very common in primary care. Ensure BOTH conditions documented at each visit with separate MEAT for each.
💡 Very common diabetic complication. SGLT2i addresses both — document both conditions separately.
💡 Diabetic nephropathy. Also triggers E11.22 (DM with CKD) — code the diabetic CKD under HCC 36 AND the CKD stage separately.
💡 Cardiorenal syndrome. Common in elderly MA patients. Document both with nephrology/cardiology co-management.
💡 HIGH-VALUE triple interaction — very common in primary care MA population. All 3 must be documented annually.
💡 Mental illness + chronic medical disease interaction. Behavioral patients with cardiac disease get additional interaction credit.
💡 Document transplant status AND any current complications, infections, or rejection episodes for full interaction capture.
Patient has 4 or more qualifying HCCs documented
💡 V28 REWARDS complexity. A patient with 6 well-documented HCCs earns MORE than the sum of parts. Every additional legitimate HCC adds value.
Patient has 10 or more qualifying HCCs documented
💡 Highest complexity tier. Ensure ALL chronic conditions are documented annually — each one contributes to the interaction bonus.
prompt_library: CLINICAL SIGNAL → PROVIDER REVIEW PROMPT LIBRARY
Signals are prompts for clinical review only. They must not be used as autonomous diagnosis-generation rules.
Domain
Signal / Evidence
Provider Consideration
Documentation to Clarify
LLM Guardrail
Diabetes
A1c/glucose abnormalities; insulin or antihyperglycemic therapy; prior diabetes diagnosis
Evaluate whether diabetes is active and whether documented complications are present.
Type, control/status, complications, treatment, monitoring and relationship to complications when clinically established.
Do not diagnose diabetes or a complication from a medication or lab value alone.
CKD
Reduced eGFR; nephrology follow-up; prior CKD diagnosis
Evaluate current CKD status and stage.
Current stage, renal function trend, treatment/monitoring and any clinically established causal relationships.
Do not assign CKD stage from a single isolated result without appropriate clinical confirmation.
Heart failure
Loop diuretic, cardiology notes, prior HF, echo findings, edema/dyspnea
Evaluate whether HF is active and clarify phenotype/acuity.
Systolic/diastolic/combined or other phenotype when supported; acute/chronic status; symptoms; treatment.
Do not infer HF from edema, diuretic use, or an abnormal test alone.
Pulmonary
Maintenance inhalers, oxygen, PFTs, smoking history, prior COPD
Evaluate active pulmonary diagnosis and severity where clinically supported.
COPD/asthma/other diagnosis, exacerbation status, oxygen dependence if applicable, treatment and symptoms.
Do not infer COPD solely from inhaler use or smoking history.
Vascular
Prior PAD/PVD, vascular imaging, claudication, ulcers
Evaluate active vascular disease and manifestations.
Anatomic site, symptoms/complications, laterality where required, treatment and surveillance.
Do not code from imaging/history alone without provider assessment of current condition.
Neurologic
Prior stroke, weakness, mobility deficits, antiseizure therapy
Evaluate current neurologic condition and residual deficits.
Etiology, residual deficit, laterality/dominance where relevant, seizure type/status, treatment.
Do not infer hemiplegia, epilepsy, or other neurologic diagnosis solely from medication/history.
Cancer
Oncology follow-up, antineoplastic therapy, prior malignancy, imaging
Clarify active disease versus history/remission and metastatic status.
Primary site, secondary sites, current treatment, remission/status and surveillance.
Do not label historical cancer as active or metastatic without documentation.
Nutrition
Weight loss, low BMI, dietitian notes, nutrition support
Evaluate for clinically established nutritional disorder when appropriate.
Clinical diagnosis, severity, supporting assessment, treatment and monitoring.
Do not diagnose malnutrition from BMI, albumin, or weight loss alone.
Wounds
Wound-care notes, pressure injury, home-health documentation
Evaluate active wound and document clinically determined characteristics.
Location, laterality, stage/severity when clinically established, treatment and progress.
Do not infer pressure-ulcer stage from non-provider shorthand or incomplete evidence.
Status conditions
Transplant, amputation, ostomy, dialysis or device history
Determine whether a status code/condition is current and clinically relevant.
Current status, complications if any, ongoing management and related active conditions.
Do not assume a complication merely because a status condition exists.

tips_warnings: CODING TIPS & DOCUMENTATION WARNINGS — HCC V28 | One Per Condition
⚠️ = Common coding errors that result in MISSED RAF or AUDIT RISK. Review with your coding/documentation team.
⚠️ Use secondary site codes (C77–C79) WITH primary site code. Do not use C80.1 if primary site is known.
⚠️ Document laterality (right/left) and lobe. Specify small cell vs non-small cell when known.
⚠️ Document "HIV disease" (B20) not just "HIV status" — specify active disease vs asymptomatic (Z21)
⚠️ Quadriplegia (G82.5x) has HIGHEST RAF in motor function category (0.890). Document level and completeness explicitly.
⚠️ Specify type: Hodgkin vs NHL vs leukemia vs myeloma. Document remission status explicitly.
⚠️ MUST document STAGE 4 explicitly — staging is clinical. Unspecified pressure ulcer (L89.x09) does NOT generate payment HCC. Photograph and measure at each visit.
⚠️ Document primary site specifically (cecum, ascending, sigmoid, rectum). Use C19 for rectosigmoid junction.
⚠️ Specify paraplegia (G82.2x) vs hemiplegia (G81.x) vs monoplegia. Document dominant vs non-dominant side for hemiplegia.
⚠️ Status epilepticus (G41.x) maps to highest-RAF epilepsy HCC (0.567). Document seizure type specifically — "convulsions unspecified" (R56.9) does NOT map to payment HCC in V28.
⚠️ G35 is the only ICD-10 code for MS. Always document current disease activity and functional status to support medical necessity.
⚠️ Must document STAGE 3. Specify anatomical site (sacrum L89.15x, heel L89.61x, etc.). Stage must be documented by clinician — cannot be assumed from nursing notes alone.
Chronic Ulcer of Skin / Non-Pressure Ulcer
⚠️ Specify ulcer type and location: lower leg (L97.x), other site (L98.4x). Diabetic foot ulcer is captured under diabetes HCC (E11.621) — do not double-code.
⚠️ Specify organism when known. R65.20/R65.21 requires underlying infection code first. Document septic shock separately.
⚠️ Document CIRRHOSIS explicitly — "liver disease" alone insufficient. Specify with/without ascites for K70.30 vs K70.31.
⚠️ Always document organ/site specifically. Confirm active vs history of cancer — history codes (Z85.x) do NOT generate RAF.
⚠️ "Anemia unspecified" (D64.9) has NO payment HCC in V28. Must specify aplastic (D61.x) or acquired hemolytic (D59.x).
Cardio-Respiratory Failure and Shock / Cardiac Arrest
⚠️ Use I46.2 (underlying cardiac condition) or I46.9 (unspecified). Document cause and survival status clearly.
⚠️ Specify schizophrenia TYPE and episode status. Schizoaffective (F25.x) maps to same HCC. Document acute exacerbation vs stable.
⚠️ Specify seropositive (M05) vs seronegative (M06). Document organ involvement for highest specificity.
⚠️ Document transplant STATUS (Z94.x) at EVERY visit — it must be recaptured annually. Kidney (Z94.0), heart (Z94.1), lung (Z94.2), liver (Z94.4). Must be active — not rejected/failed.
⚠️ Use G40.x codes — specify intractable vs not intractable, with/without status epilepticus. Unspecified codes generate lower or no RAF.
⚠️ V28 KEY SPLIT: Severe MDD (F32.2, F32.3, F33.2, F33.3) generates RAF 0.396. Mild/moderate = lower RAF 0.214. MUST document severity with PHQ-9 score.
⚠️ Document DEPENDENCE (F10.2x) for highest RAF vs abuse (F10.1x). Must specify with/without withdrawal or intoxication.
⚠️ Specify substance: opioid (F11.x) has distinct codes. Document DEPENDENCE vs abuse. "Opioid use disorder" must map to F11.2x for payment.
⚠️ Use Z89.x codes — specify level (below-knee Z89.51x, above-knee Z89.61x, etc.) and laterality. Must document ACQUIRED amputation — congenital absence is different code.
⚠️ Specify type — sickle cell disease (D57.x) carries high RAF. Must document crisis status when applicable.
⚠️ Use I63.x for ischemic stroke (highest RAF). I64 for unspecified. TIA (G45.x) does NOT map to stroke HCC. Document neurological deficits at each follow-up visit.
⚠️ HIGH VALUE: Must document SPECIFIC behavioral disturbance — "with agitation" (F01.511), "with psychotic disturbance" (F01.52). Plain "dementia" = lower RAF.
⚠️ Specify COPD (J44.x) not just "lung disease" — J44.1 (with acute exacerbation) is most specific. Emphysema (J43.x) and chronic bronchitis (J41-42) also map to same HCC.
⚠️ OSA alone (G47.33) does NOT generate payment HCC in V28. Must have OBESITY HYPOVENTILATION (E66.2) with hypercapnia confirmed on ABG. Different from OSA.
⚠️ Specify SYSTOLIC (I50.2x) vs DIASTOLIC (I50.3x) vs COMBINED (I50.4x). Document ACUTE vs CHRONIC. Acute on chronic = highest acuity code.
⚠️ MOST COMMONLY MISSED HCC in primary care (RAF 0.302). Specify: GAD (F41.1), panic disorder (F41.0), PTSD (F43.10/F43.11), OCD (F42.x). "Anxiety NOS" (F41.9) still valid but use specific code.
⚠️ Use G20.A1/A2 (without dyskinesia) or G20.C1/C2 (with dyskinesia). Old code G20 alone still valid but less specific.
⚠️ Document viral type (B18.0, B18.1, B18.2). Cured HCV does NOT generate RAF — must be active or chronic.
⚠️ Must use CHRONIC DVT codes (I82.x1/x2/x3) — acute DVT codes are different. Specify laterality and vessel.
⚠️ Document STEMI vs NSTEMI vs subsequent MI (I22.x). Within 4 weeks = acute MI. After 4 weeks = use "old MI" or CAD codes.
⚠️ Document SUSTAINED vs unsustained VT. I47.21 (sustained VT) is most specific. VFib (I49.01) maps to same HCC.
⚠️ Always document CURRENT episode type. "Bipolar unspecified" (F31.9) still maps but be specific: manic (F31.1x), depressed (F31.3x), mixed (F31.6x).
⚠️ F84.0 (autistic disorder) and F84.5 (Asperger's) both map. Document LEVEL of support required (Level 1/2/3) per DSM-5.
⚠️ Must document ESRD (N18.6) or Stage 5 (N18.5) explicitly. Dialysis dependence = Z99.2. Any of these maps to HCC 326 (RAF 0.280).
⚠️ Document severity using PHQ-9 score. "Depression NOS" or "depressive disorder unspecified" (F32.A) may no longer qualify. Specify mild (F32.0) or moderate (F32.1).
⚠️ Only paranoid (F60.0) and schizoid (F60.1) currently map to payment HCC. Other personality disorders may not generate V28 RAF.
⚠️ Use E66.01 for morbid obesity. General obesity (E66.09, E66.9) may not meet threshold. Also code BMI (Z68.4x).
⚠️ Document dementia TYPE (Alzheimer's G30.x, Lewy Body G31.83, Vascular F01.x, Frontotemporal G31.0x). "Senility" or "cognitive decline" insufficient for HCC.
⚠️ Document stenosis LOCATION specifically: carotid (I65.2x), vertebral (I65.0), cerebral (I66.x). Specify laterality. Sequelae of stroke (I69.x) also maps.
⚠️ V28 CRITICAL: CAD WITHOUT angina (I25.10) no longer maps to a payment HCC. MUST document angina symptoms to use I25.11x codes.
⚠️ Always document AFib TYPE: paroxysmal (I48.0), persistent (I48.11/I48.19), permanent (I48.21). Unspecified (I48.91) still valid but be specific.
⚠️ DKA (E1x.10/11) and hyperosmolarity (E1x.00/01) are ACUTE complication codes = HCC 35. Same RAF as HCC 36/37 in V28 (constrained). Still important to document accurately.
⚠️ V28 CONSTRAINT: HCC 36 (chronic complications) = same RAF 0.166 as uncomplicated DM. STILL document complications for accurate clinical picture and comorbidity interactions.
⚠️ Even "uncomplicated" diabetes generates RAF 0.166 in V28. Always specify TYPE (E10=Type1, E11=Type2, E08=underlying condition, E09=drug-induced).
⚠️ I73.9 (PVD unspecified) is valid but document symptoms: claudication, rest pain, tissue loss for higher specificity.
⚠️ N18.4 (Stage 4 CKD) = RAF 0.137. Must use the specific stage code — "CKD unspecified" (N18.9) does NOT generate payment HCC in V28.
⚠️ G31.84 (mild cognitive impairment) and F06.70/F06.71 qualify. "Memory loss" unspecified (R41.3) does NOT map to HCC in V28.
⚠️ Only Stage 3b (N18.32) maps to HCC 328. Stage 3a (N18.31) and Stage 3 unspecified (N18.30) do NOT generate payment HCC in V28.
guardrails: COMPLIANCE & AUDIT GUARDRAILS FOR LLM USE
Clinical truth and documentation integrity control all recommendations. Use official current coding/model guidance for final coding and payment decisions.
Topic
Rule
Safe LLM Response Pattern
Escalate / Verify When
Unsupported diagnosis
Do not assign or recommend an active diagnosis that is not supported by the encounter documentation.
“The record suggests a possible issue for provider review; the available information is insufficient to establish the diagnosis.”
Evidence is conflicting, historical, copied forward, or absent from assessment/plan.
Medication inference
Medication use may have multiple indications.
“This medication may prompt review of its indication; confirm the underlying condition with the provider.”
The indication is not explicit.
Lab inference
Abnormal labs are evidence, not necessarily a coded diagnosis.
“Consider clinical evaluation of the abnormal result and document the provider’s diagnosis if established.”
A diagnosis/stage would be derived from an isolated or ambiguous result.
Problem lists / prior claims
Prior data can identify potential recapture gaps but does not prove current disease.
“Previously documented condition—confirm whether it remains active and is addressed this year.”
Current encounter does not substantiate the condition.
Causal linkage
Do not create causal relationships unless coding rules or provider documentation support them.
“Clarify whether the conditions are clinically related before selecting a combination/manifestation code.”
Diabetes complications, hypertensive relationships, manifestations, or etiology are unclear.
Specificity
Never add stage, severity, laterality, acuity, complication or status without support.
“Specificity is missing; request provider clarification.”
More specific code materially changes HCC/payment or clinical meaning.
History vs active
Distinguish active disease, remission, history, and status.
“Confirm current disease status before using an active-disease code.”
Cancer, infection, acute disease, or prior events are mentioned historically.
RAF values
Coefficients and payment effects depend on model/year/segment/demographics and other factors.
“Workbook RAF values are reference estimates; verify against the applicable CMS model.”
A payment, forecast, audit, or contractual decision depends on the number.
Official validation
The workbook is a secondary reference.
“Validate final code/model eligibility against current official CMS and ICD-10-CM guidance.”
There is a conflict, model-year change, code-set update, or high-impact decision.
